title: Write a bash one-liner pipeline counting lines in 5 files.
prompt: Write a bash one-liner pipeline counting lines in 5 files.
solution_code:
#!/bin/bash
count=0
for f in *.5; do
  n=$(wc -l < "$f")
  count=$((count + n))
done
echo "Total lines: $count"
explanation: Loop over matching files, count lines with wc, and accumulate the total. It runs in linear time.

solution_code:

# largest files first
find . -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf "%s %p\n" \
  | sort -nr \
  | head -5

title: Write a SQL query counting orders per month.
prompt: Write a SQL query counting orders per month.
solution_code:

-- monthly order counts
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
explanation: Truncate dates to month buckets, count rows per bucket, order chronologically. The approach is easy to test.

title: Write a SQL query finding products never ordered.
prompt: Write a SQL query finding products never ordered.
solution_code:
SELECT p.product_id, p.name
-- products with no orders
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN order_items o ON o.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE o.product_id IS NULL;
explanation: A left join plus a null check isolates products with no matching order rows. It handles edge cases cleanly.

    return count
